Routing Preference
Distance Correction
If your own routing software (NetPas, sea-distances.org, etc.) consistently shows longer/shorter distances than this tool, enter the % difference here (e.g. +6 if this tool reads 6% short). It scales every auto-routed and hand-drawn leg — manual overrides are left untouched, since those are already your known-correct number. Sea days, bunker cost, hire days, and cost/tonne all update with it.

Draw a Custom Route (optional)

Traces the sea lane by hand for maximum accuracy — click points on the map between the two ports, then Finish. Use MarineTraffic or the OpenSeaMap overlay (map layers icon) to see real Traffic Separation Schemes before you click.

Set up your rotation and variables, then hit Calculate Voyage.

Distances route through the Eurostat SeaRoute / MARNET maritime network (8,400+ real waypoints, github.com/eurostat/searoute, EUPL-1.2), with canal and strait passages (Suez, Panama, Malacca, Gibraltar, Bab-el-Mandeb, and others) identified from the dataset's own tagging rather than hand-picked node clusters — plus a small number of supplementary waypoints added and geographically verified where that network's real coverage had a gap. The Avoid Piracy Zone toggle covers the Gulf of Aden / Somali Basin corridor specifically; it is not an official designation (the industry's old fixed "High Risk Area" was retired in 2023) and the actual current risk picture shifts — check current UKMTO/BIMCO/IMB guidance rather than relying on this alone. Selecting a Vessel Type pre-fills Consumption, Port Duty, and Freight Rate from a tanker chartering reference sheet — every pre-filled number is a normal editable field, not a locked value, and coverage is partial (not every port or route pair has reference data). Bunker prices are still placeholders — replace with current MABUX/Platts prices. The map defaults to a nautical chart basemap — use the layers icon top-right to switch to a standard map or turn on OpenSeaMap's shipping-lane/buoy overlay for tracing manual routes more precisely. Canal transit dues, agency fees, and anything not covered by Port Duty should be folded into "Other Costs".
